post.caption:
Even releasing every bit of accessible CO2 on Mars, in the ice caps and the soil, falls far short of a breathable atmosphere at anything like Earth pressure. And the planet could not keep one: no global magnetic field means the solar wind strips the upper atmosphere, and gravity is about a third of ours. The soil also carries perchlorates that are toxic to people. Domes and buried habitats are plausible this century. Planet-wide terraforming is a multi-century problem with unsolved physics.
